According to the Census of India 2011, the national male workforce participation rate (WPR) for all ages was 53.26%.

Further insights:

• The female workforce participation rate (FWPR) as per Census 2011 was 25.51%.

• Workforce participation rate is defined as the percentage of the total population (or population of a specific age group) that is either working (employed) or seeking work (unemployed but available).

• These rates vary by age group, rural/urban areas, and educational levels.

• According to the Census 2011 provisional reports, India's population in 2011 was 1,210,854,977 (1.21 billion), compared to 1,028,610,328 in 2001. The population increase is:

○ 1,210,854,977 − 1,028,610,328 = 182,244,649 (approximately 182.2 million).

○ This is more than 181 million.

• Decadal Growth Rate (2001 - 2011): The Census 2011 reports a decadal growth rate of 17.64% (or 17.7% in some sources), compared to 21.54% in 1991 - 2001. The decline is:

○ 21.54% − 17.64% = 3.90 percentage points

• Post-Independence decadal growth rates (from Census data):

○ 1941 - 1951: 13.31%

○ 1951 - 1961: 21.51%

○ 1961 - 1971: 24.80%

○ 1971 - 1981: 24.66%

○ 1981 - 1991: 23.87%

○ 1991 - 2001: 21.54%

○ 2001 - 2011: 17.64%

• The 3.90% decline from 1991 - 2001 to 2001 - 2011 is the largest drop in decadal growth rate since Independence, surpassing previous declines (e.g., −2.33% from 1981 - 1991 to 1991 - 2001).

• The growth rate of population is defined as the change of population expressed in percentage.

• The decadal growth rate of population refers to the percentage change in a region's population over a ten-year period. It is calculated by comparing the population figures at the beginning and end of the decade, determining the absolute increase, and then expressing this increase as a percentage of the population at the start of the decade. ​

• India's decadal growth rate for 2001-2011 was approximately 17.68%.

India's population growth rate has decelerated to 17.64 per cent in the decade 2001-11, the slowest rate of growth this past century, according to the first results of Census 2011 put out by the registrar-general of census.

According to the Census of India 2011, Serchhip district in Mizoram has the highest literacy rate in India at 97.91%. This small district outperformed others due to strong educational initiatives in the state of Mizoram, which overall has high literacy.

· "Champhai" (option 1), also in Mizoram, has a literacy rate of 95.91%, lower than Serchhip.

· "Idukki" (option 3) in Kerala has 91.99%, and "Ernakulam" (option 4), also in Kerala, has 95.89% - both high but below Serchhip.

Kerala and Mizoram dominate literacy rankings, but Serchhip tops the list, making option 2 the correct answer.

· According to the Census 2011, the sex ratio of India, defined as the number of females per 1,000 males, was 943.

· The same for rural and urban areas are 949 and 929 respectively.

Further Insight:

· The sex ratio for 0-19 age group was 908 while that of 60+ age group was 1033. The sex ratio in the economically active age group (15-59 years) was 944.

· The sex ratio was highest in Kerala (1084) followed by Puducherry (1037) and lowest in Daman & Diu (618) followed by Dadar & Nagar Haveli (774) and then Chandigarh (818).

· Over the last 60 years (Post Independence) considerable improvement in sex ratio was observed in Andaman & Nicobar Islands (40.16%), Delhi (13.02%), Assam (10.34%) and West Bengal (9.82%).

· However, the situation has worsened in the major States of Bihar (-8.21%) and Odisha (-4.23).

The 15th National Census survey conducted by the Census Organisation of India was held in 2011.

Census has been conducted in India since 1872 and 2011 marks the first time biometric information was collected. The motto of the census was Our Census, Our Future.

The population of the country as per the provisional figures of Census 2011 is 1210.19 million of which 623.72 million (51.54%) are males and 586.46 million (48.46%) are females.

• As per the Census 2011, Nagaland recorded the lowest population growth rate among Indian states.

• Nagaland experienced a negative population growth rate of -0.58%, primarily due to out-migration and possible over-reporting in the previous census.

• This was a significant deviation from the national growth rate of 17.64%.
As per the Census of 2011, Meghalaya achieved the highest decadal growth rate of 27.9% during the period from 2001 to 2011.

· Sikkim, with a population of approximately 6.1 lakh (Census 2011), had the lowest population among Indian states.

· The 15th National Census of India was conducted in 2011.

· The official slogan for the 2011 Census of India was: "Our Census, Our Future".

· It was the 7th census after independence (1951, 1961, 1971, 1981, 1991, 2001, 2011).
